project.name: Forge
project.description: Spec-driven development system powered by AI agents. Plan → Execute → Verify with quality gates at every step.
project.architecture: TypeScript modulith on Bun. Monorepo with packages/ (domain libraries, adapters, CLI) and apps/ (desktop UI).
key_packages: contracts - Plan schema and validation (JSON Schema 2020-12)
guidance-pack - Workflow policy, rules, and skills (generated assets)

stack.serving_model: Single-origin SPA: Fastify serves API routes + Vite build output
anti_patterns: Do not use Tailwind — Vuetify handles component styling
Do not use Nuxt or SSR — single-origin SPA only
Do not use Bun-native APIs (Bun.serve, Bun.file) — use Node-compatible APIs for portability
Do not use decorators — use plain functions and constructor injection
Do not use `any` — use `unknown` with type narrowing

module_layout: index.ts — barrel exports of public API only
container.ts — exports registerXModule(container) for DI registration
services/ — business logic classes with constructor injection
domain/ — types, schemas, validation; no infrastructure imports
architecture.barrel_export_rule: Cross-module imports go through index.ts only
architecture.di_pattern: registerXModule(container) in container.ts, called from composition root; use asClass().scoped() for request-scoped services
architecture.route_pattern: routes.ts default-exports RouteRegistrar (async Fastify plugin); resolve services via diScope
architecture.shared_types: Framework contracts (RouteRegistrar) in shared/types.ts; module types via barrel exports

rules: NEVER write production code without a failing test. Tests come first, always.
The spec phase produces RED tests — they must fail before any implementation.
The implement phase produces GREEN tests — write only the minimum code to pass.
The refactor phase keeps tests GREEN — improve structure without changing behavior.
Each phase ends with its gate passing AND a commit. No silent phase transitions.
If a gate fails, fix the issue in the current phase. Do not advance.
If spec-phase tests pass immediately, the specification is too weak — strengthen it.

property_test_taxonomy: round-trip — encode then decode returns original
idempotence — applying operation twice equals applying once
invariant — property holds for all valid inputs
oracle — compare implementation against simple reference
no-invalid-state — constructor/factory never produces invalid state

testing_patterns.black_box: Test public interfaces at every level; avoid reaching into private implementation
testing_patterns.build_test_app: Use buildTestApp() to create a configured Fastify instance for integration tests

gates.spec: bun run typecheck && bun run test
gates.green: bun run test && bun run typecheck && bun run lint
gates.refactor: bun run test && bun run typecheck && bun run lint
gates.verify: bun run test:coverage && bun run typecheck && bun run lint && bun run architecture:check

skills.name: plan-author
skills.description: Create or revise Forge plan artifacts with dependency-aware tasks, explicit tests metadata, and documentation updates. Use when planning or re-planning work before implementation.
skills.default_prompt: Draft or revise a Forge plan with complete task metadata, dependencies, verification commands, and documentation updates.
instructions: Keep every task small enough for deterministic execution and review.
For each non-documentation task, include at least one code-first BDD scenario.
Describe property and contract tests when applicable; use empty arrays only if not relevant.
Prefer fakes over mocks in planned tests; reserve mocks for adapter boundaries and failure simulation.
Always include documentation updates and decision notes for each task.
Use verification commands that can run unattended in CI.

skills.name: spec-bdd
skills.description: Author failing specification tests in code-first BDD style for Forge tasks. Use when implementing the Spec step before writing production code.
skills.default_prompt: Write failing tests first using Given/When/Then comments and align them to plan acceptance criteria.
instructions: Write failing tests before implementation changes.
Use Given/When/Then comments in test bodies.
Favor behavior-focused assertions over implementation detail coupling.
Use fakes by default; only use mocks for adapter boundaries or explicit failure simulation.
When using mocks, annotate each call site with // forge-mock: adapter_boundary or // forge-mock: failure_simulation.
Run the spec gate command after creating tests.
If tests pass before implementation, strengthen the specification.

skills.name: implement-green
skills.description: Implement the minimum code to satisfy Forge test gates while preserving modulith boundaries. Use during implementation and refactor phases.
skills.default_prompt: Implement the smallest change set that turns failing tests green and passes architecture checks.
instructions: Implement domain-first and preserve module boundaries.
Avoid introducing any or bypassing lint/type checks.
Keep test doubles fake-first; allow mocks only for adapter boundaries and failure simulation.
If a mock is unavoidable, annotate call sites with // forge-mock: adapter_boundary or // forge-mock: failure_simulation.
Run green and refactor gates after implementation updates.
Keep public APIs stable unless the plan explicitly includes a breaking change.
Record constraints discovered during implementation in decision notes.

skills.name: document-and-decide
skills.description: Update task documentation and decision records to match implementation. Use during the documentation phase before commit.
skills.default_prompt: Update docs and decision notes so they accurately describe implemented behavior and interfaces.
instructions: Update affected docs files and keep wording implementation-accurate.
Update decisions.md with rationale for meaningful technical decisions.
Ensure public interfaces include concise documentation comments.
Run the docs gate after documentation edits.
Reject completion if code and documentation diverge.
